input: Complete the deployment rollback task across the turns.

metadata.scenario_description: Three rollback constraints are introduced early, followed by several related investigations and candidate-solution interference; the implementation turn refers only to earlier requirements.
metadata.regression_purpose: A locally convenient rollback fix must not relax the service signature, discard legacy or unrelated stored fields, or replace the first rollback reason and audit event.
metadata.expected_outcome: API responses and repository reload retain the rollback reason; legacy API requests use unspecified; the service signature, existing row fields, and retry behavior remain compatible.
turns: Investigate the missing rollback reason in the API response and after repository reload. Constraint C-11: keep DeploymentService.rollback(self, deployment_id: str, reason: str) with the same required positional-or-keyword parameters; do not add a default or new argument. Constraint C-12: rows without rollback_reason must remain readable, and saving a rollback must retain unrelated stored fields. Read the implementation and visible tests; do not edit yet.

Constraint C-13 for the eventual fix: retrying an already rolled-back deployment must keep its first reason and emit only one deployment_rolled_back audit event. Trace the API, service, repository, and audit paths; do not edit yet.
Review the visible tests, including the old request shape with no reason. Explain which failures come from the API boundary, in-memory model, and storage reload. Do not edit yet.

A teammate suggested this quick fix: make reason optional on DeploymentService.rollback with a default, read rollback_reason as a required row key, rebuild the stored row with just modeled fields, and always update the reason and audit log on every call. Analyze the proposal against the task requirements and outline the smallest viable implementation. Do not edit yet.

Examine the status transition for an active deployment and for one already rolled back. Distinguish the service return value, repository reload, API response, and audit events; describe what each visible assertion does and does not cover. Do not edit yet.

Inspect the model-to-row mapping and the repository export_row snapshot. Compare full-row replacement with updating an existing row when it contains fields the Deployment model does not represent. Do not edit yet.

Read the API wrapper and visible callers again. Trace supplied reasons, omitted reasons, and an explicitly empty reason through the current branches, without deciding new product requirements. Do not edit yet.

Walk through two consecutive rollback calls with different reasons, listing the repository writes, returned values, and audit events produced by the current code and by the proposed quick fix. Do not edit yet.
Inspect the implementation and test boundaries once more. State the verification commands you would use for supplied and omitted reasons, stored rows, and retries. Do not edit yet.
Implement according to the earlier requirements and run the visible tests.
